title: Reductive groups admit pinned split realizations etale locally
statement: Let $A$ be any nonzero commutative ring and $G$ a reductive group over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, with reductivity and pinned split realizations defined in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. There exist a set $J$, nonzero commutative $A$-algebras $C_j$, and etale morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}C_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] whose images jointly cover $\operatorname{Spec}A$, such that $G\times_A C_j$ [def-pc-fibre-product] admits a pinned split realization of a finite reduced based root datum $\mathcal R_j$ for every $j\in J$. The lattice, rank and based datum may vary with $j$. Neither $A$ nor $C_j$ is required to be Noetherian. No finiteness of $J$ and no integral model is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3 and Proposition 5.1.6, printed pp.136-138; Definition 6.1.1 and its following paragraph, p.186; affine localization of the etale neighborhoods Read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-parameter-scheme] to $G/A$. Its representing scheme $Q\to S$ is a smooth surjection. By [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections], applied to this scheme regarded as an algebraic space by its representable sheaf with the identity etale atlas [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] (so $Q\to S$ is smooth on that chart and surjective on field-valued point classes), take an etale covering $U_i\to S$ and lifts $U_i\to Q$. The representing bijection gives a maximal $U_i$-torus in $G_{U_i}$. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-etale-trivialization] to each of these tori, and refine the resulting sources by nonempty affine open neighborhoods. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], open inclusions and the successive etale maps compose to etale maps. We obtain an affine etale covering $\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to S$ with specified split maximal tori $D_{B_i}(M_i)\hookrightarrow G_{B_i}$. All indices range over sets. Each $B_i$ is nonzero since its spectrum is nonempty.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3, first two sentences of proof, p.137; Corollary 3.2.7, p.95; Proposition B.3.4, pp.291-292.

proof.text: Every group obtained by the base changes and open refinements used here remains reductive. Indeed smoothness is preserved by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], affineness by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], and finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. For any chart algebra $B$ and homomorphism $B\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field, $(G_B)_\Omega=G\times_A\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for the composite $A\to B\to\Omega$. This is one of the geometric fibres required to be connected reductive by [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Thus all subsequent applications of the relative reductive-group input have the required hypotheses. A split maximal torus pulls back to a closed subgroup by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change], and its fibrewise maximality pulls back to the corresponding geometric fibres.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3, p.137, passage to base changes; definition of reductivity, Definition 3.1.1.

proof.text: Fix one chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with lattice $M$, choosing a basis $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. By [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] its tangent module is finite projective, its zero-weight module is $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$, and each nonzero weight has fibre dimension zero or one. Its dual-number module agrees with [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]: the Hopf counit identities make first-order terms add under group multiplication, and $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ scales their derivations by $a$. The coaction weight condition $\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m$ implies $\operatorname{Ad}(t)(v_R)=\chi_m(t)v_R$ by evaluation at each algebra point $t:B[M]\to R$. Conversely use $R=B[M]$ and the universal torus point given by its identity map; the tangent base-change comparison identifies that equality with the coaction equation. Thus these are exactly the full-torus weight modules in the current definition. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] to its conjugation coaction: there are only finitely many nonzero weight summands, and their ranks are simultaneously locally constant. Around each point shrink to an affine open on which all these ranks are constant. Let $\Phi\subset M\setminus\{0\}$ be those of rank one there; the other nonzero weight modules vanish. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to each of the finitely many rank-one summands and intersecting the resulting neighborhoods makes all $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ free of rank one. The decomposition is now $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Each shrinking still contains its chosen point, so these choices cover the original chart.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3, middle sentence of proof, p.137; Section 4 introduction, pp.107-108; choose trivializations as required in Definition 5.1.1(2).

proof.text: For each $\alpha\in\Phi$, [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] provides a relative coroot $\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_m\to T$. By [lem-sfb-relative-split-torus-matrix-sheaf] its exponent vector is locally constant with values in $M^\vee$. At any point intersect the constancy neighborhoods for the finitely many $\alpha$, and choose a nonempty affine neighborhood inside the intersection. Then every coroot is a constant monomial cocharacter on this neighborhood. The root modules remain free with the previous generators restricted. Their base-change compatibility identifies the roots in every geometric fibre with the same $\Phi$, and the coroots with the same vectors $\alpha^\vee\in M^\vee$. We have not assumed that any neighborhood or the original base is connected.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.3, final sentence of proof, p.137; Definition 5.1.1(3), p.136.

proof.text: On one final nonempty affine chart choose a geometric point. The prescribed split torus becomes a maximal torus $T$ over its algebraically closed field. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] choose a Borel pair $(T_0,B_0)$ in this fibre. By [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] conjugate $T_0$ to $T$, thereby obtaining a Borel subgroup containing $T$. The root-datum and simple-base assertions of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] identify the lattice, roots and canonical coroots at this point with a finite reduced root datum and supply a base $\Delta\subseteq\Phi$. The geometric coroots used here are the rank-one $\operatorname{SL}_2$ coroots of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], which states their diagonal formula and uniqueness for the rank-one reflection, exactly as the current realization definition requires. All its root-datum identities, including the reflection and reducedness conditions, are identities in the fixed integer lattices. Step 4 identifies the same vectors at every geometric point. Hence this one fibre verifies those identities for the constant data on the whole chart. No constancy of the residue characteristic is needed. The empty-root case gives $\Delta=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 5.1.6, first sentence of proof, p.138; Definition 6.1.1, p.186.

proof.text: For each $\alpha\in\Delta$ choose a generator $X_\alpha$ of the already free rank-one module $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. The torus, constant roots and coroots, decomposition and these generators satisfy exactly [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], so they give a pinned split realization of the based datum from step 5. Let $J$ index all the nonempty affine neighborhoods used in the preceding refinements, with coordinate rings $C_j$. The refinements cover every source chart; their composites cover $S$ and are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Each $C_j$ is a nonzero commutative $A$-algebra. This gives the asserted family, allowing a different lattice and datum on each chart; the construction imposes no Noetherian condition and produces no integral model.

source.place: Definition 6.1.1 and following paragraph, p.186; affine refinements of Lemma 5.1.3.
